raw_response:
I've farmed these same two mu for 50 years. Never went to school, but I know this land. It's just me now — one mouth to feed, but I still need the grain for eating and a little cash for salt and medicine. I can't spend much. Every yuan I put into the ground is a yuan I don't have in my pocket if something goes wrong.

**Wheat** — I plant in the first week of October, same as always. I saved my own seed from last year's harvest, about 5 kg per mu. Cleaned it myself, didn't buy nothing. Before planting I spread one big bag of compound fertilizer across the two mu — that's half a bag per mu, about 25 kg. I plow it in with the small tiller. In the spring, when the wheat starts growing fast and looks a bit yellow, I walk to the shop and buy half a bag of urea, maybe 12 kg per mu, scatter it by hand. That's all the fertilizer I can afford. Water costs money — the pump takes electricity — so I irrigate three times: once before winter so the wheat doesn't dry out, once when it's jointing around Qingming, and once when the grain is filling. I spray herbicide once in early spring, that's it. No insecticide unless I see bugs. I do all the work myself — planting, fertilizing, watering, spraying, harvesting. Takes me about two weeks of work spread across the season. I expect maybe 380 kg per mu if the weather is normal. Not great, but enough to make flour.

**Maize** — After wheat comes off in early June, I got maybe five or six days to get maize in the ground. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, about 2 kg per mu, costs me 25 yuan per mu. Can't save maize seed, everyone knows that. I put down fertilizer at planting — maybe 20 kg per mu of compound fertilizer. If the plants look hungry in July, I topdress a little urea, maybe 10 kg per mu. Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat. I'll irrigate twice — once at planting if it's dry, and once at flowering. Three times only if it's a bad dry year. I spray herbicide after planting, and insecticide once if I see armyworms. Harvest is late September. Another ten days or so of my labor. I hope for about 420 kg per mu.

I don't hire nobody. Can't pay them. At 68 I move slower than before, but I know the rhythm of the year. I don't try new varieties or new methods. Last year was okay, so I do the same this year. Better to waste a little fertilizer than to risk an empty stomach.
